speaker: priest
english: Grant, Lord, that what we have taken with our mouth, we may receive with a pure mind, that of a temporal gift it may become to us an eternal remedy.
notes: Runs over the page break at xlii/xliii; only the tail (`of a temporal gift ... remedy.`) stands on xliii, so this row overlaps the preceding lane, which owns xlii and the rubric `Taking the first Ablution, he says,` that heads the block. Scan damage on xlii: the first line prints `that wha` with only the top serif of the terminal t surviving at the right margin; read whole against the facing Latin `Quod ore sumpsimus`.

english: Taking the second Ablution, he says,
notes: Italic, centred across the full measure above both columns.

speaker: priest
english: May thy body, O Lord, which I have received, and thy blood which I have drank, cleave to my bowels; and grant, that no stain of sin may remain in me, who have been fed with this pure and holy sacrament. Who livest and reignest, &c.
notes: `have drank` is the book's form. The conclusion is abbreviated `Who livest and reignest, &c.` where the Latin column sets it out in full, `Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.` Right margin clean on this leaf.

english: Then he returns to the Book, and reads the COMMUNION, which may be seen in its proper place.
notes: Italic, set across the full measure and turned over two lines; `COMMUNION` is in small capitals and is broken `COMMU-` / `NION` at the turn. The book gives no Communion antiphon text here, only this cross-reference.

speaker: priest
english: The Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit. Let us pray.
notes: Three lines set as one block in both columns; only the response carries `R.`, the priest's parts being unmarked. `Oremus.` / `Let us pray.` is centred on its own line within the same block.

english: From Candlemas-day till Passion Sunday, and from the III. Sunday after Pentecost until Advent, (except on Doubles and within Octaves) after the proper POSTCOMMUNION, the following is the
notes: Set across the full measure with roman and italic alternating word by word: the named seasons and feasts are roman, the connective matter italic. `POSTCOMMUNION` in small capitals. Ends without punctuation, running straight into the heading of the next block.

speaker: priest
english: II. POSTCOM. (Mundet.) May the oblation of this divine sacrament, we beseech thee, O Lord, both cleanse and defend us; and by the intercession of the blessed Mary the Virgin Mother of God, of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, of blessed N. and of all the saints, free us from all sin, and deliver us from all adversity.
notes: Set across the full measure with NO facing Latin column; `latin_incipit` is therefore empty, but the book supplies its own Latin cue as the parenthesis `(Mundet.)`, which is italic. `II. POSTCOM.` is roman full capitals and is part of the printed paragraph, so it is transcribed here.

english: From Low Sunday, exclusively, till the Ascension, instead of the foregoing, is said the P. COMM. * Sumptis, &c. as in the Votive Mass SALVE for the B. V. M. p. 509.
notes: Set across the full measure, roman and italic alternating as in row 6. `COMM.` in small capitals, `SALVE` in full capitals. The asterisk after `P. COMM.` is printed on the page but has NO answering footnote anywhere on xliii, which is blank below this point but for the following rubric.

english: After the Postcommunion, is added the following
notes: Set across the full measure in ROMAN, not italic, unlike every other rubric in this range; it is the last thing printed on xliii and its sentence is completed by the heading at the head of xliv.

english: PRAYER. (Et famulos.)
notes: Centred at the head of xliv across the full measure. `PRAYER.` roman full capitals, `(Et famulos.)` italic; the parenthesis is the book's own Latin cue for a prayer it prints in English only.

speaker: priest
english: DEFEND also, O Lord, from all adversity, thy servant N. our Pope, N. our Bishop, together with the people committed to his care: grant peace in our days, and banish all wickedness from thy Church: thro', &c.
notes: Two-line drop D, transcribed as an ordinary capital; `EFEND` is in full capitals beside it. Set across the full measure with NO facing Latin column. The book prints a blank line after `our Bishop,` and then a blank space of about an inch within the line, between `people` and `committed`; inspected at 1000 dpi and there is no ink there at all, so the gap is the book's own setting, not scan loss.

speaker: priest
english: The Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit. Go, you are dismissed, (or) let us bless the Lord. R. Thanks be to God.
notes: The book sets the greeting and the dismissal as ONE block with no break: Latin `Dominus vobiscum. / R. Et cum spiritu tuo. / Ite missa est (vel) Benedicamus Domino. / R. Deo gratias.` The English renders `Ite missa est` as `Go, you are dismissed,` and gives the alternative in the same sentence as `(or) let us bless the Lord.` No rubric governs the choice between them.

english: In Masses for the Dead.
notes: Italic, centred across the full measure.

speaker: priest
english: P. May they rest in peace. R. Amen.
notes: Both columns print `P.` and `R.`, unlike the two preceding dialogues. `Amen.` is italic in both columns. Scan damage: `in` of `rest in peace` prints as `iu`, the n having lost its right stem at the column edge; read against the facing Latin `Requiescant in pace`.

english: Bowing before the Altar, the Priest says
notes: Italic, centred across the full measure. It ends with NO terminal comma, where every other `he says` rubric in this range takes one; checked at 1000 dpi.

speaker: priest
english: Let the performance of my homage be pleasing to thee, O holy Trinity; and grant that the sacrifice which I, tho' unworthy, have offered up in the sight of thy Majesty, may be acceptable to thee, and thro' thy mercy be a propitiation for me, and all those for whom it has been offered. Thro'
notes: The English column ends on the bare word `Thro'` with no full stop and no `&c.`, where the facing Latin sets the conclusion out in full, `Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.` Checked at 1000 dpi: nothing follows `Thro'`, and it is not a case of lost ink. `tho'` and `thro'` are the book's spellings.

english: Turning himself towards the People, he gives them his Blessing, saying,
notes: Italic, set across the full measure and turned over two lines.

speaker: priest
english: May Almighty God, the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, bless you. Amen.
notes: `kind` is `form` as the closest of the five permitted values; it is the blessing formula, not an oration. Set across the full measure in English ONLY: there is no Latin `Benedicat vos omnipotens Deus`, and the single cross sign the Latin rite prescribes is printed in NEITHER column, no cross glyph appearing anywhere on this opening. `Amen.` is italic.

speaker: priest
english: P. Our Lord be with you. R. And with thy spirit. P. The beginning of the Gospel according to St. John. R. Glory be to thee, O Lord.
notes: Runs over the page break at xliv/xlv. The Latin opens `P. Dominus vobiscum.` and continues `P. Initium sancti Evangelii, secundum Joannem. R. Gloria tibi, Domine.` This greeting is rendered `Our Lord be with you`, against `The Lord be with you` at rows 5 and 12 of the same range. The book prints no rubric for signing the book, the forehead, the lips or the breast.

speaker: priest
english: IN the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God: the same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him, and without him was made nothing that was made; in him was life, and the life was the light of men: and the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.
notes: `kind` is `prayer` as the closest of the five permitted values; this is a Gospel lection, not an oration. Two-line drop I in both columns, transcribed as an ordinary capital, with `N` in full capitals beside it. The book divides the last Gospel into three paragraphs which the two columns keep aligned, and this is the first. Scan damage: `the` in `in the beginning` prints as `thc` and `ning` in `beginning with God` prints as `nmg`, both broken types rather than margin loss; read against the facing Latin `hoc erat in principio apud Deum`.

speaker: priest
english: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to give testimony of the light, that all men might believe through him. He was not the light, but was to give testimony of the light. That was the true light which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world.
notes: Second of the three paragraphs of the last Gospel; both columns break here. `through` is set out in full, where the same book abbreviates to `thro'` elsewhere on this opening.

speaker: priest
english: He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not. He came unto his own, and his own received him not. But as many as received him, to them he gave power to be made the sons of God: to them that believe in his name, who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God: And THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH, and dwelt among us; and we saw his glory, as it were the glory of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
notes: Runs over the page break at xlv/xlvi. `THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH` is in small capitals, the run beginning after the roman `And` and ending at `FLESH`, the following comma and `and dwelt` returning to roman; the facing Latin sets `VERBUM CARO FACTUM EST` in the same small capitals, beginning after the roman `Et`. NO rubric about genuflecting is printed at this point in either column, nor anywhere in the last Gospel; the small capitals are the only mark the book makes of the place. Scan damage: `be` in `power to be made` has lost the bowl of its b; read against the facing Latin `dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri`.

speaker: server
english: R. Thanks be to God.
notes: The last thing printed above the rule that closes the Ordinary. Set as its own block, indented, after a blank line; the Latin column prints `R. Deo gratias.` opposite. Immediately below it runs a thick-and-thin double rule across the full measure, and below that rule xlvi is entirely blank to the foot of the page.
